claims.rule: Preserve class-wrapper capture at command granularity: retain required earlier-command instances and exclude wholly unused commands, not individual unused fields inside a retained instance. For ordinary captured values and a serializable retained reachable graph, an independent-classloader round trip must not rerun their initialization.
claims.applicability: Observed in the 2018 Scala 2 class-wrapper implementation and strengthened by a separate 2019 isolated-loader test revision. A 2021 guard disables the suite on Scala 3. Re-establish closure lowering and prerequisites rather than copying Ydelambdafy. Inference: the retained reachable graph must remain serializable; same-command sibling exclusion is not promised. Result assertions, literal-lookalike and cache-restore controls are proposed stronger oracles, not all historical assertions.
claims.counterexample: If captured a and nonserializable d share one required Helper, retaining d is not an introduced violation of the historical command-pruning contract. Intentional singleton references and object-only macro definitions retain distinct semantics; do not add field-level closure cleaning or universal serialization incidentally.

claims.rule: Derive used-command names from typed compiler dependencies and carry structured metadata with compilation/session state, not rendered-tree regexes or opaque classpath resources. Inference from PR 944: preserve both term selections and type-derived references before nulling earlier commands; receiver-symbol matching alone does not make a term-only collector complete.
claims.applicability: Structured metadata is explicit 2018 review guidance. The 2019 TypeTree/SingleType extension and evaluator regression are source-backed inference, not a reviewer preference: PR 944 has only release coordination and approval comments. Its Mill build uses Scala 2.11.12/2.12.8 primary cells; rediscover compiler internals and test dispatch on Scala 3. Preserve cache/session association; stale tree.txt comments do not describe final behavior.
claims.counterexample: Generated source strings remain appropriate for emitting wrappers, but not for inferring symbol use.
